name: Lake Kel-Suu
near: There are no permanent villages nearby: the base is the yurt camps in the Kok-Kyya valley (≈20 yurts, end of the road; about 8–12 km on foot to the lake). The last sizeable settlement is At-Bashy; the city of Naryn is 150–200 km by road (sources disagree). The earlier “Karaul-Tobe ~38.5 km” is a straight-line distance across the mountain ridges and is no guide for the trip.
elev: About 3500 m (too.kg, Kabar, kgnomad); TripAdvisor says 3520 m, the Trip to Kyrgyzstan catalogue 3514 m. Water level and surface area change noticeably from season to season and year to year.
short: Kel-Suu is a narrow turquoise lake at ~3500 m in a rocky canyon near the Chinese border (At-Bashy District), with a vanishing water level and boat rides between sheer walls.
desc: The lake lies in a narrow canyon between sheer cliffs in the southeast of Naryn Region, about 20 km from the Chinese border, and feeds the Kok-Kyya River. Its length varies by source from 9 km (too.kg) to ~12 km of canyon (Kabar) and 17 km (TripAdvisor); the width ranges from a few dozen metres to 2 km. Kabar links the lake's formation to a landslide in the 1980s, while kg24.news calls it a glacial water body in a fissure; what they agree on is that the water periodically drains into underground grottoes and the level changes dramatically (the last big drop was in 2018), hence the Kyrgyz “kel-suu” — “coming water”. In summer the water is 8–10 °C, and the weather changes within minutes: sun, rain, wind, hail. Access is only with a border permit, through the checkpoint after the Kyndy Pass and the yurt camps in the Kok-Kyya valley. With the growth in tourist numbers in 2026, litter has become a problem (time.kg, 14.08.2026), and the Ministry of Transport checked boatmen for registration and documents (24.08.2026).
guide: The main thing at Kel-Suu is a motorboat ride deep into the canyon: the walls rise straight out of the turquoise water, and only from the water do you see how long the lake really is. Head to the lake in the morning — the fords on the Kok-Kyya rise by 30–50 cm after lunch, and dozens of people gather at the shore by midday. Look at the dark caves in the cliffs: according to local stories, the lake's water drains into underground grottoes from time to time, which is why it looks different every year. Don't be surprised if you find it lower than in photos — that's normal. Take your litter with you: in 2026 the shores became noticeably dirtier, and locals are talking about it.
see: A canyon with sheer walls and turquoise water — best seen from a motorboat (30 min — about 1000 som/person, 2024–2025); caves and grottoes in the cliffs; the ford and the Kok-Kyya river valley with yaks; the ~8–12 km footpath (2–3 h one way) from the camps to the lake; the road via Ak-Say and the Kyndy Pass (3400 m).
skip: You have fewer than 3 full days from Bishkek (5 from Almaty) — the road will take almost all your time. You can't get the border permit in time (from a few working days to 2 weeks). You don't tolerate an altitude of ~3500 m and cold nights down to −5 °C in a yurt without amenities.
diff: Moderate: the road is difficult (4×4 jeep, fords), while the walk itself is ~12 km round trip with almost no elevation gain (OunTravela) with a river ford; alternatively, ride a horse or take a UAZ “bukhanka”/GAZ-66 for the last ~8 km. The main difficulties are the 3500 m altitude, the weather and the river level.
when: Mid-July to late August (NomadCar); the yurt camps operate from about late June to early September (kgnomad; too.kg — mid-June to early September). Snow is possible in June, nights are frosty in September, and the road is impassable in winter. The lake level is higher in July–September (TripAdvisor).
hours: An open natural area, but only with a border permit; the camps operate seasonally (late June — early September). The permit is checked at the post after the Kyndy Pass.
daytime: Morning: there is less water in the Kok-Kyya River (after lunch the level rises by 30–50 cm — NomadCar), fewer people at the lake (TripAdvisor), and calmer water for the boat. Leave the camp at dawn.
how: Bishkek → Naryn (≈350 km of paved road) → At-Bashy → Kyndy Pass (3400 m) and the border post → Ak-Say valley → Kok-Kyya valley (end of the road, yurt camps). From there it is 8–12 km to the lake on foot, on horseback or by UAZ/GAZ-66. From Naryn to the camps it is 150–200 km over gravel and fords, 4–8 h (Kabar: 150–160 km, 5–6 h; OunTravela: ~200 km, 4–5 h; NomadCar: 120 km of gravel + 60–80 km of fords). The total journey from Bishkek is 10–12 h.
needcar: Yes: a 4×4 SUV is a must (ground clearance of 200–220 mm or more, low-range gear) with a local driver, or a tour; there is no public transport.
self: Partly: you can arrange the permit yourself through CBT Naryn or tour.too.kg, but driving without an experienced local driver and a prepared 4×4 is not recommended (fords, no signal, difficult navigation — Freedom Travel 2025). The walk from the camps can be done on your own (sea2peak, no guide).
roadtype: Paved up to Naryn; Naryn — At-Bashy — Kyndy — Ak-Say is gravel/washboard (≈120 km); the last 60–80 km have boggy stretches and fords (NomadCar). In August 2026 road maintenance unit no. 20 of At-Bashy District graded the At-Bashy — Kyndy — Torugart road (time.kg). The last 8–12 km to the lake are a trail and a ford.
traveltime: Bishkek — Naryn ~5–6 h; Naryn — Kok-Kyya camps 4–8 h (OunTravela 4–5 h; Kabar 5–6 h; kgnomad 5–8 h); camp — lake 2–3 h on foot one way. From Almaty to Ak-Say — 15–16 h (Freedom Travel, 07.2025). At least 3 days from Bishkek.
stay: Yurt camps in the Kok-Kyya valley: Kel-Suu Yurt Camp (2GIS: from 1800 som, up to 40 beds, breakfast, cafe, horse rides, Wi-Fi; +996 552 979 696; rating 4.7/30), Golden Moon (often mentioned — kgnomad), Jyrgal's Yurt Camp (video). 2024 prices (too.kg): a yurt for 2 with breakfast — 1700 som/person, a yurt for 4–7 — 1500 som/person, a “hotel” room with breakfast — 2000 som/person, meals — 800 som per meal; kgnomad (2026): 1500–2500+ som/person with meals. Tent camping is possible (sea2peak).
net: There is practically no mobile signal after leaving Naryn/the last villages (NomadCar, too.kg, kgnomad 2026); a weak signal sometimes on the passes. Some camps have Wi-Fi (Kel-Suu Yurt Camp per 2GIS; Kabar) — probably satellite, quality not confirmed.
entry: No separate entrance fee for the lake was found. A border permit is mandatory: CBT Naryn — €30 (Naryn Region only, 1 week), €35 (several regions), €50 rush in 2 working days; tour.too.kg — 3000 som (all border zones, 7 working days, 2026); too.kg (2024) — 2600 som for a foreigner, 3–4 working days.
transfer: Jeep Naryn — Kok-Kyya — Naryn with waiting: 13,000–20,000+ som per car (≈3500–5000 som/person with 4 passengers, kgnomad 07.2026). UAZ/GAZ-66 to the lake: 10,000 som per group round trip (too.kg 2024). Marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek — Naryn — 600 som (CBT Naryn, 05.2026). A 3-day group tour from Bishkek — from 14,900 ₽ (tour.too.kg, 2026).
bring: Your border permit (original/printout) and passport; a warm jacket and hat (down to −5 °C at night, hail by day), a rain jacket; sunscreen and sunglasses — sunburn is common (Freedom Travel); shoes for the ford or sandals; cash in som (no ATMs); a flashlight, a power bank; a bag for litter; a first-aid kit including altitude-sickness remedies.
warn: Border zone next to the Chinese border: without a permit you will be turned back at the post after the Kyndy Pass. The Kok-Kyya River rises 30–50 cm after lunch, and the ford is impassable during floods (NomadCar, Freedom Travel) — cross in the morning. Altitude ~3500 m, abrupt weather changes, water 8–10 °C. Only get into boats with life jackets: in 08.2026 some boatmen turned out to have no documents (time.kg). There is no signal. The lake level can be low — photos online don't guarantee the view.
food: The yurt camps serve simple home cooking: beshbarmak, shorpo, boorsok, kaimak, tea, sometimes kumis (meals ~800 som each — too.kg 2024). On the way — lagman at a cafe in Naryn (Freedom Travel, 2025).
reviews: TripAdvisor: 4.9/5, 43 reviews, no. 1 of 15 in Naryn (as of 07.10.2026). Google Maps: 4.8/5, 99 ratings (as of 03.10.2026, catalogue cross-check). 2GIS — Kel-Suu Yurt Camp: 4.7/5, 30 ratings. Pros — “the most beautiful place”, turquoise water, a boat ride through the canyon, the road via Ak-Say. Cons — a long, hard road, low water levels in some seasons, crowds in peak season, litter (2026).
p.sum: Kel-Suu is in the border zone by China: first arrange a permit (tour.too.kg 3000 som/$35 or CBT Naryn €30–50, 5–7 working days), then allow 2–3 days: Naryn → At-Bashy → Kyndy Pass (2 border posts) → Ak-Say → the Kok-Kyya yurt camps (≈145–160 km, 4.5–6 h by 4×4). You spend the night in a yurt (1500–2500 som with meals), and in the morning go 7.5–9 km on foot, on horseback (≈2000–2500 som) or by UAZ (10,000 som/car) to the lake and take a boat ride through the canyon (≈1000 som/30 min). The easiest option is a group tour with tour.too.kg ($195 from Bishkek) or a 2-day tour from Naryn; on your own — only with a local driver and a full tank from Naryn.

p.iti.0.title: 2 days from Naryn
p.iti.0.plan: Day 1: 9:00 departure from Globus (Naryn) → At-Bashy → Kyndy (posts) → Ak-Say → lunch/evening in a Kok-Kyya yurt (≈5 h on the road). Day 2: 7:00 breakfast, in the morning (while the water is low) 2–3 h to the lake on foot/horseback/UAZ, a 30-min boat ride, a picnic; 13:00 back to camp, 14:00 departure, ≈19:00 Naryn.
p.iti.1.title: 3 days from Bishkek
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: 08:00 Bishkek → Boom Gorge → Orto-Tokoy → lunch in Naryn → evening at the Kok-Kyya camp (≈460 km). Day 2: the lake (hike/horse/boat). Day 3: back via Bozogo, lunch in Naryn, evening in Bishkek (tour.too.kg itinerary).
p.iti.2.title: A logical combination
p.iti.2.plan: Kel-Suu + Kok-Kyya valley + Ak-Say (one road) → on the way back Koshoy-Korgon (near Kara-Suu) → Tash-Rabat and Chatyr-Kol (with the same permit) → Naryn → Song-Kol via Dolon/Kalmak-Ashuu. 6–8 days as a loop (like the Journal of Nomads overland tour “Kel Suu, Tash Rabat and Son Kul”).
p.iti.3.title: From the west via Chatyr-Kol
p.iti.3.plan: Tash-Rabat → the Bishkek—Kashgar highway → along Chatyr-Kol → Ak-Say valley → Kok-Kyya: 205 km in a day (Nomad's Land) — with one permit it combines Tash-Rabat, Chatyr-Kol and Kel-Suu without returning to Naryn.
p.season: June: snow is possible, the camps open toward the end of June, high water at the fords. July — August: the best time, the lake is full, the camps are open, +15…+20 by day, around 0 °C at night, hail. September: camps until ≈25.09, night frosts, few people, lower water. October — May: the Ak-Say road is under snow (down to −40…−56 °C), since 2025 there has been a winter festival in February, in winter only organized groups. Few mosquitoes, but horseflies near the herds.
p.budget.economy: ≈14,000–18,000 som/person for 3 days in a group of 4: marshrutka Bishkek—Naryn 600×2; jeep Naryn—Kok-Kyya—Naryn 13,000–20,000 som/4 ≈3500–5000; permit 3000; yurt 2 nights with breakfast and dinner ≈3000–4200 (1500–2100/night, JoN 2026); horse 2000–2500 or walking 0; boat 1000; a night in Naryn ~1500–2500.
p.budget.comfort: ≈$195–350 for a tour (tour.too.kg group tour $195 from Bishkek or JoN €230–350 from Naryn) + horse ~$20 + boat ~$15 + lunches ~$10 = ≈20,000–35,000 som/person.
p.permits: A border permit is mandatory (border zone of At-Bashy District by the Chinese border). Ways to get it: 1) tour.too.kg — 3000 som (all border zones) / $35 for the Kel-Suu—Kok-Kyya—Chatyr-Kol zone; 5–7 working days; office at 105/3 Isanov St., Bishkek (2026). 2) CBT Naryn — €30 (Naryn Region only, ~1 week), €35 (several regions), €50 rush in 2 working days (stage 1); Nomad's Land: from Naryn it is quickest — within a few days, via Bishkek — up to 2 weeks. Step by step: (1) send a scan of your passport and your travel dates (WhatsApp/form); (2) pay a 50% prepayment; (3) the Border Service reviews it for ~1 week; (4) pick up the paper original in Bishkek or Naryn (or via a guide/tour — in which case a copy of your passport is sent several days ahead). The permit is valid for up to 1 month. It is checked at the military posts at the Kyndy Pass/at the entrance to the Ak-Say valley (2 posts per Eurasia Travel) — you need the original permit with a stamp, and your passport. Photographing the posts is prohibited. No entrance fee for the lake/valley was found. JoN (04.2026) advises applying for the permit through CBT Naryn at least 2 weeks ahead; if you travel on your own, your driver needs a permit too.
p.access: With children — only school-age and if they tolerate altitude well (3500 m, 5–6 h of bumpy road, fords); Tripster writes “not suitable for children”. For older people — hard because of the road and altitude; you can reach the lake by UAZ. With a stroller — not accessible. With a dog — technically possible in your own car, but not recommended in the border zone and among shepherd dogs.
